{{Short description|none}} {{Use mdy dates|date=September 2021}} {{use American English|date=September 2021}} {{Infobox election | election_name = 2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Nebraska | country = Nebraska | type = legislative | ongoing = no | previous_election = 2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Nebraska | previous_year = 2020 | next_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Nebraska | next_year = 2024 | seats_for_election = All 3 Nebraska seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = November 8, 2022 | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | last_election1 = 3 | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | swing1 = | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | last_election2 = 0 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | swing2 = | map_image = | map_caption = }} {{ElectionsNE}} The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Nebraska''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the three [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Nebraska]], one from each of the state's three [[Nebraska's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with the [[2022 Nebraska gubernatorial election|Nebraska gubernatorial election]], as well as other elections to the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|U.S. House of Representatives]], [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]], and various [[2022 United States elections|state and local elections]]. Nebraska's primary elections took place on May 10. {{toclimit|2}} == District 1 == {{Infobox election | election_name = 2022 Nebraska's 1st congressional district election | country = Nebraska | type = presidential | ongoing = yes | previous_election = 2022 Nebraska's 1st congressional district special election | previous_year = 2022 (special) | next_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Nebraska#District 1 | next_year = 2024 | image_size = x150px | image1 = Mike Flood 117th Congress (cropped).jpeg | nominee1 = [[Mike Flood (politician)|Mike Flood]] | party1 = Republican Party (US) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = Patty Pansing Brooks (cropped).jpg | nominee2 = [[Patty Pansing Brooks]] | party2 = Democratic Party (US) | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Mike Flood (politician)|Mike Flood]] | before_party = Republican Party (US) | after_election = | after_party = }} {{see also|Nebraska's 1st congressional district}} The 1st district is located in eastern Nebraska surrounding [[Omaha, Nebraska|Omaha]] and its suburbs, taking in [[Lincoln, Nebraska|Lincoln]], [[Bellevue, Nebraska|Bellevue]], [[Fremont, Nebraska|Fremont]], and [[Norfolk, Nebraska|Norfolk]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Mike Flood (politician)|Mike Flood]], who was elected with 52.7% of the vote in a [[2022 Nebraska's 1st congressional district special election|2022 special election]] after the previous incumbent, [[Jeff Fortenberry]], resigned March 31, 2022 after having been indicted and convicted on charges of lying to the FBI about campaign donations.{{cite web |title=General Election Official Results |url=https://sos.nebraska.gov/sites/sos.nebraska.gov/files/doc/elections/2020/2020-General-Canvass-Book.pdf |website=Nebraska Secretary of State |access-date=December 4, 2020}} === Republican primary === ==== Candidates ==== ===== Nominee ===== * [[Mike Flood (politician)|Mike Flood]], incumbent U.S. representative{{Cite web|last=Walton|first=Don|date=January 16, 2022|title=Flood challenges Fortenberry, says indictment puts House seat at risk|url=https://journalstar.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/flood-challenges-fortenberry-says-indictment-puts-house-seat-at-risk/article_d2c49949-faa5-5f80-a9d7-8bb3eb7b7e9e.html#tracking-source=home-just-in|url-status=live|access-date=January 16, 2022|website=[[Lincoln Journal Star]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220116230919/https://journalstar.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/flood-challenges-fortenberry-says-indictment-puts-house-seat-at-risk/article_d2c49949-faa5-5f80-a9d7-8bb3eb7b7e9e.html |archive-date=January 16, 2022 }} ===== Eliminated in primary ===== * John "Glen" Weaver, [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] veteran{{Cite web|title=Air Force veteran announces bid for Nebraska's 1st Congressional District|url=https://www.ketv.com/article/air-force-veteran-announces-bid-for-nebraskas-1st-congressional-district/38991114|access-date=February 5, 2022|website=www.ketv.com|publisher=[[KETV]]|language=en-US}} * Thireena Yuki Connely, teacher * Curtis D.
